text: In eighteen forty-seven, one Vienna hospital ward was losing nearly one in five new mothers. Doctor Ignaz Semmelweis noticed something. Doctors were walking from dead bodies straight into the delivery room. So he told them to wash their hands in chlorine. Deaths fell from eighteen percent, to about two. But the doctors laughed. They rejected him, and he died in an asylum in eighteen sixty-five, forgotten. Today, the World Health Organization says clean hands can prevent up to half of avoidable hospital infections. He wasn't selling soap. He was selling life.
